title: Two-frequency ratios reduced hidden-cell bias but raised median sampling error in 11 of 12 selected linear-model tests
abstract: We tested a two-frequency estimate of direct connection ratios in partially observed real linear circuits. Independent local noise probes remove unknown input powers and diagonal cell filters. A real-coefficient expansion shows that two frequencies cancel the leading hidden-path bias for four nonzero direct weights. Exact error then has fourth-order rather than second-order frequency decay. In fixed worm, fly and Allen-based mouse graph models, extrapolation reduced exact error in 6,271 of 6,300 selected ratio-frequency cases. Fifty signed synthetic models and a closed-form example supported the derivation. Equal-cost spectral sampling gave a different result: extrapolation had higher median error in 11 of 12 settings in one synthetic circuit. The package includes code, proof, aggregate scores, synthetic trials, figures, input hashes and external retrieval steps. No animal activity was analyzed. Unknown fast hidden dynamics, weak denominators, model error and sampling noise limit practical use.
